correctness.rationale: Reconstructed seven transient states, recovery/infection rates and five symmetry-reduced Perron equations. The unique positive QSD exists for λ>0. Exact adjugate/resultant identities exclude all competing mode crossings; the λ=2 artifact has θ=3 outside (0,1). Derivatives at λ=3/4 give strict ordering on both sides. A Sturm sequence isolates exactly one eligible second crossing, and positive balance identities exclude the disconnected pair. Standalone checker recomputed algebra, independent 7-state generator and numerical spot checks; no finite sample is substituted for the analytic all-λ argument.

value.rationale: The center of a minimal nonregular contact network is initially the single most likely infected state; the modal structure then changes to a pair and finally full infection, with an exact five-way degeneracy and a nontrivial algebraic second threshold. This is a natural finite-network benchmark for QSD and conditional-risk approximations, different from standard expected prevalence or extinction time. Finite exactness alone is not its motivation; the structural modal reordering and all-rate boundaries are.
